newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam unveils restructuring, big job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam unveils restructuring, big job cuts.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp., the appliance maker led by corporate turnaround specialist Albert Dunlap, said Tuesday it would cut 6,000 jobs, or half its work force, in a major restructuring.
Dunlap, known as "Chainsaw Al" for his deep cost-cutting at troubled corporations, promised to overhaul Sunbeam within a year when he was named chairman in July.
Sunbeam said it would slash product lines and cut its facilities to 14 from 53, and take a charge of $300 million to pay for one-time costs associated with the plan.
The job cuts were larger than early reports had indicated. The New York Times said Tuesday that as many as 4,000 jobs could be cut.

Last month, the maker of Sunbeam and Oster appliances, patio furniture and gas grills reported its first quarterly loss since selling stock to the public in 1992. It also announced that it would unveil a restructuring in the week of Nov. 11.
The Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based firm said it lost $28.7 million in the third quarter, as sales fell 2 percent to $245.0 million from the 1995 quarter.
Shrinking profit margins and high manufacturing and administrative costs have depressed profits in recent years. Sunbeam earned $50.5 million in 1995, or less than half of its 1994 profits.

Dunlap, who was named chairman and chief executive officer in July, is credited with turning around Scott Paper Co., which was later sold to Kimberly-Clark. At Scott Paper, Dunlap fired 10,000 workers and sold more than $2 billion in assets.
While his turnaround campaigns have helped stockholders, they have also been criticised by community activists, unions and other groups as insensitive to workers.
Within months of joining Sunbeam, Dunlap replaced several top executives and brought in people who had worked for him in the past.
Sunbeam's stock was halted by the New York Stock Exchange prior to the announcement. It was unchanged at $25.75.
The company said it would hold a conference call with Wall Street analysts on Tuesday afternoon to discuss the plan.
